subject: Regional traffic shield validation & customer action required
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jones <sam.jones@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional traffic shield validation & customer action required

Hi Sam / Acme ops team —

We detected elevated 5xx error rates and connection failures for requests routed to our eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 endpoints starting ~08:42 UTC this morning. Root cause investigation is ongoing (cloud provider interconnect degradation impacting NAT/egress paths) and our SREs have implemented an automated traffic shield to prefer US regions while we stabilize the interconnect.

What changed (short):
- Traffic for affected tenants is being routed to us-west-2 / us-east-1 variants by default where compatible model variants exist.
- We elevated prefix/KV cache retention to reduce the need for cold-start token rebuilds during the shift.
- Fallback: if request latency to US regions exceeds your threshold, we will return a 503 with consumer-friendly guidance rather than degrade correctness.

What we need from you (action items):
1) If you have a region-override in client config, please update your request host to api.redwood.ai?region=us or set X-Preferred-Region: us to opt into the shield immediately.
2) Validate your rate-limit windows for the US endpoints — we recommend a one-time burst allowance for 30 minutes while traffic is migrated.
3) Confirm the attached temporary-routing-config.yaml applied successfully (reply with the validation CSV attached).

ETA and next steps:
- Short-term mitigation is active. We expect the provider to start capacity recovery in the next 2–4 hours; we will watch for full restoration and advise rollback to normal affinity.
- We will send a post-incident summary and an explicit rollback window once the interconnect is healthy.

Attached: temporary-routing-config.yaml, traffic-shield-checklist.pdf (checks for application teams).

I know this is disruptive — we’re prioritizing minimizing error rates and avoiding silent correctness regressions. Please reply with your validation status or any constraints that prevent applying the override.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0152
From: Sam Jones <sam.jones@acmelogistics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional traffic shield validation & customer action required

Thanks Hannah —

On our side we see increased 502/504s from eu-west endpoints since 08:45 UTC. We can flip the override but two quick clarifications before we do:
- Will routing to US regions affect token billing or per-token latency significantly for our workflows (image-to-text + summarization pipeline)?
- Can you confirm there will be no model-variant downgrades when moving to US regions (we use a tuned quantized variant in eu-west).

Ops will stand by to apply the temporary-routing-config.yaml once we get confirmation.

Sam
Sam Jones
Platform Lead, Acme Logistics
ops@acmelogistics.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: quick tech notes for Acme apply + rollback window

Internal notes (please keep internal-only):

- Billing: routing to US regions will not change per-token invoicing unit; token accounting is centralized and region-agnostic. Customers may see slightly higher latency (p90 + 40–120ms) depending on client round-trip; cost impact negligible for short-term migrations.

- Model variants: we mapped model hashes across regions. For Acme's tuned quantized variant we have an identical build available in us-west-2. No downgrade expected. If the customer is using a proprietary pinned binary without cross-region variant, we will automatically select the closest compatible quantized variant and tag the response with X-Model-Variant-Warn.

- Operational commands (for SRE/CS team to share with customer):
  1) Apply temporary-routing-config.yaml (attached) to your client config. Example curl: 
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/apply-routing 
       -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
       -d @temporary-routing-config.yaml
  2) Verify endpoint: curl https://api.redwood.ai/health?region=us -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
  3) Upload reroute-validation.csv to the ticket (HUBSPOT-123456) with a sample of requests and latency.

- Rollback: once provider confirms restored interconnect, set region override to auto-affinity and run the health probe. Planned rollback window will be communicated in the postmortem.

Vanessa (cc Hannah for customer comms)
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jones <sam.jones@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional traffic shield validation & customer action required

Sam —

Thanks for the quick questions and for standing by. Short answers:
- Token billing: no change — accounting is region-agnostic. We will not double-bill or change unit tokens during the reroute.
- Model variant: your tuned quantized build exists in us-west-2; we will preserve the same variant hash. We will include the variant hash in the response header X-Model-Variant so you can validate.

We recommend applying the temporary-routing-config.yaml now. Vanessa has included the SRE-safe curl examples above. If you want we can apply the override for you from our side (we would need a short-lived service account key and explicit opt-in).

Next steps and follow-up:
- Please upload reroute-validation.csv after you run the check (we attached an example template).
- We will publish a post-incident summary within 48 hours and a final postmortem in 5 business days. Draft postmortem will be shared with your security/compliance team for review.

Apologies again for the disruption. Please tell us whether you want Redwood to apply the override or if you will push from your side.

Best,
Hannah
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (preliminary), reroute-validation.csv (template)
snippet: Regional interconnect issue impacting eu/apac — temporary traffic shield to US regions. Customer action: apply override or request Redwood to apply; postmortem to follow.
